chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: May a woman wash her husband's private part? He said, "Why? Is it due to illness?" I said, "No." He said, "I do not like for a free woman to do that; as for a bondwoman, it does not harm him." He said: I said to him, "May a man perform ghusl in the presence of his family?" He said, "Yes; what he exposes in intimacy is greater."

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman; here, the wife being asked about
key_terms.بَيْنَ يَدَيْ أَهْلِهِ: in the presence of his family

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a wife to wash her husband's private part, and may a man perform ghusl in front of his family?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses etiquette and legal considerations related to washing the private parts and performing ghusl within the household. It indicates a distinction in what is considered disliked in domestic conduct while affirming the permissibility of a man performing ghusl before his family.
